name: Git and the Command Line
description: Keep every version of your work, and share it on GitHub.

lessonObjectives.l1-every-version: See what problem version control solves, and what a commit records.
lessonObjectives.l2-first-commit: Initialise a repository, stage a file and commit it.
lessonObjectives.l3-staging-area: Use the staging area to commit exactly the changes you mean.
lessonObjectives.l4-reading-history: Read the log and the difference between two commits.
lessonObjectives.l5-on-a-branch: Create a branch, switch to it and commit there.
lessonObjectives.l6-merging: Merge a branch and read what the merge did.
lessonObjectives.l7-collisions: Resolve a merge conflict by hand.
lessonObjectives.l8-undoing-safely: Choose between restore, revert and reset for each kind of mistake.
lessonObjectives.l9-pushing: Connect a remote and push your work.
lessonObjectives.l10-asking-for-review: Open a pull request from a branch.
lessonObjectives.l11-pipes: Chain shell commands with pipes and redirect output to a file.
lessonObjectives.l12-keeping-secrets-out: Write a `.gitignore` for data files and keys, and check it works.
